As of v3.4.1, when `init.redirect` is `'follow'`, the default, redirects are followed as the Fetch Standard specifies. A `301` or `302` response to a `POST`, and a `303` response to any method other than `GET` or `HEAD`, make the next request a `GET` with no body, and drop the `Content-Encoding`, `Content-Language`, `Content-Length`, `Content-Location`, and `Content-Type` headers. Any other redirect sends the body again, which fails with `NETWORK_ERROR` when the body is a stream. A redirect to another origin drops the `Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Host`, and `Proxy-Authorization` headers. Before v3.4.1, every redirect resent the original method, body, and headers, and a redirect to another origin dropped only `Authorization`.

As of v3.4.1, the response body is decoded when `Content-Encoding` lists `gzip`, `x-gzip`, or `deflate`, including several of them applied in turn, and is left as received when it lists any other coding. Before v3.4.1, only a single `gzip` or `deflate` was decoded, and a `deflate` body came out wrong.

from: - `NETWORK_ERROR` — the underlying request failed or the connection was lost.
to: - `NETWORK_ERROR` — the underlying request failed or the connection was lost, or, as of v3.4.1, a redirect would have to send a streamed body again.
